answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, externally costly bond before it may submit bids, then slash that bond when independent audits prove fraud. Splitting one attacker’s stake across many identities does not create more voting weight or payout: each new account needs its own locked capital, and detected Sybils lose it. Audits can compare signed transaction histories across a ferrous supply chain, using a karst mine’s shipment records as a prism for spotting duplicated claims. The defense raises the attacker’s cost in proportion to the influence they seek.
